children: The rupee opened 15 paise higher on September 1, after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) was said to be intervening in the market, which offset the weaker sentiment emanating from higher Brent crude prices and a stronger US dollar.
The local currency was trading at Rs 95.01 per dollar, as compared to Rs 95.16 per dollar in the previous trading session. The rupee had hit a two-week high on Monday.

The RBI was active in the spot market on Monday, having sold at least $5 billion, according to traders. Moreover, the MSCI rebalancing of stocks on Monday was said to have garnered at least $1 billion in inflows, which helped the rupee appreciate to Rs 95.11 per dollar.
The currency's resilience was further supported by India's strong Q1 FY27 GDP growth of 7.8 percent.

However, market participants are also worried about the escalation of geopolitical tensions in West Asia between the United States and Iran, which has again led to renewed fears. Brent crude prices were trading at $91 per barrel.

Meanwhile, the RBI’s special concessional swap window for foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR-B) deposits came to an end on Monday, with traders looking forward to the final count of inflows through the route. Recent RBI data showed that more than $65 billion has been garnered through this route.
The RBI’s forward book will also be a point of concern, as it ballooned to $137 billion as of July, compared to $103 billion in June

“The pair appears to have found a strong near-term base around Rs 95.10 – Rs 95.20. While MSCI-related inflows have provided temporary support, sustaining gains below this zone may prove difficult. On the upside, Rs 95.80 remains the immediate resistance,” Amit Pabari, managing director at CR Forex Advisors, said.

title: Rupee opens 15 paise higher to Rs 95.01 per dollar, RBI intervention in focus
